title: 1958 AHSME Problem 39
statement: We may say concerning the solution of \(|x|^2+|x|-6=0\) that:

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: the sum of the roots is \(1\)

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text: the sum of the roots is \(0\)

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: the product of the roots is \(4\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text: the product of the roots is \(-6\)

solutions.text:
Let \(u=|x|\ge0.\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} u^2+u-6&=0,\\ (u+3)(u-2)&=0. \end{aligned} \] The nonnegative solution is \(u=2,\) so \(|x|=2\) and \(x=\pm2.\) Their sum is \(0.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Factor the resulting quadratic in \(u\), then translate the admissible value back to \(x\)
